chunks: From him, from Ayyub ibn Nuha and Sindi ibn Muhammad, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who was an agent/employee and died, and some of his children were taken for what was upon him, so they were fined a penalty. They went to his house and sold it, and with them were other heirs, women and men, who had not requested the sale nor were they consulted in it. Is there anything upon them regarding those? He said: 'If indeed he acquired the house from that work, and they were fined in that work, then it is upon them all.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on heirs selling a deceased agent's property without consulting all other heirs?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that when an agent's acquired property is encumbered by debts or penalties arising specifically from his agency, the resulting sale by some heirs binds all co-heirs, regardless of their consent. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the source of the debt determines its distribution among heirs, ensuring that the specific liability attached to the asset follows the asset itself rather than being treated as a general personal debt of the deceased.
